explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/657: must an n-point set in ℝ² with no isosceles triangles (every 3 points determine 3 distinct distances) determine at least f(n)·n distinct distances for some f → ∞? The statement asserts ∃ f → ∞ with f(n)·n ≤ #distances for every isosceles-free n-set; degenerate (collinear) isosceles triples are included, as per 'every subset of 3 points'. Faithful.
